note.en: What you see: Pressed flat under the rib edge and aimed at the left shoulder, the probe uses the liver to look up at the heart. The four chambers beat in the distance with the bright pericardium wrapping them. In health the layers glide together with no dark gap. In tamponade a dark fluid ring separates the layers and the right sided chambers collapse in diastole. Epicardial fat can mimic fluid, but fat moves with the heart wall while fluid stays still.

steps.en: What you see: Pressed flat under the rib edge and aimed at the left shoulder, the probe uses the liver to look up at the heart. The four chambers beat in the distance with the bright pericardium wrapping them. In health the layers glide together with no dark gap. In tamponade a dark fluid ring separates the layers and the right sided chambers collapse in diastole. Epicardial fat can mimic fluid, but fat moves with the heart wall while fluid stays still.
Landmarks to confirm: Heart with four chambers, pericardium, pericardial space, liver as the window.

Common mistakes and correction: Epicardial fat pad mistaken for fluid: fat is brighter and moves with the wall, fluid is dark and still. Bowel gas wiping out the heart from too steep an angle: flatten the probe and use more liver. Forgetting the liver window so the heart never appears: slide right until liver fills the near field, then aim up.

Normal values with units: No numeric threshold applies in this view. In health no dark gap separates the pericardial layers and all chambers fill in diastole. Any new circumferential dark ring with diastolic collapse of a right sided chamber suggests tamponade and needs immediate senior review.

Pitfalls: A small early effusion may show in only one fan position, so sweep the full heart before calling it negative. In chest trauma with shock and a tense circulation, a positive subxiphoid view changes management at once. Record tamponade signs frame by frame for the reviewer rather than relying on memory.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Place the probe subxiphoid, pressed flat with the marker to the right. Aim toward the left shoulder and ask the patient to bend the knees to relax the belly. Increase depth until the heart appears above the liver. Fan slowly to open all four chambers. If bowel gas blocks the view, slide slightly right onto more liver and retry. Judge fluid only when the pericardium is seen fully around the heart.
